Gillian Slovo’s play, lifted mostly from survivors’s statements and public records, shines a glaring light from which one cannot hide.
Even so, it’s a long evening, and at the close Slovo gives in to the temptation to evangelise in a J’Accuse, using videotaped testimony from the residents.
The first act drags, the second act refuses to end, and the cast size, every one of them a protagonist, creates a barrier to empathy.

Gillian Slovo’s proficiency in novel writing gives an added depth to the piece as she weaves together fact and narrative, information and emotion, causing the piece to hit just right and to grip the audience for the full three hour run time.

cn.t: Critics give this Grenfell survivor docudrama a mixed but largely respectful reception—praising its powerful performances and emotional weight, while some question whether it adds new insight beyond prior tellings of the tragedy.

vr.q: one of the best theater pieces in New York right now
